note: Adapted from the species description of Amicotermes galenus in Sands (1972), originally in English: the species lacks soldiers; the alate is described from a queen specimen only, whose coloration was noted as possibly faded; the diagnostic characters are discussed only in the generic account, so no separate diagnostic section is given. Measurement-table headers, figure numbers and locality records are not translated, and figures damaged by OCR in the measurement tables are omitted.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule and pilosity yellow, setae rather sparse, inconspicuous. Postclypeus strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.33, Pcl/Ri 3.28. The worker abdomen appears to be of the dehiscent type.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Described from a queen only, the coloration possibly faded; head capsule dark brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle flat, briefly elliptical, pale yellow, about half the size of the ocellus; median spot circular, flat, slightly smaller than the fontanelle, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus brown, labrum yellow; frontal marking semicircular, flat, brown; antennae pale yellowish brown. Pronotum brown, meso- and metanotum yellowish brown, femora and tibiae yellow, tarsi paler. Abdominal tergites yellowish brown, dorsolateral spiracles paler, sternites pale yellowish brown, ventrolateral spiracles and the middle of the sternites paler; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of the head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli of medium size, separated from the compound eye by slightly less than their own least diameter; postclypeus strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.33, posterior margin a rather angular arc, median suture distinct. Cephalic pilosity very dense, yellowish brown, slightly uneven, almost felted but concealed by numerous projecting setae.
